task.name: redesign the mobile web page
task.prompt: I don't like the current mobile web page - the task cards take up way too much space. Redesign it: - The task list should be a compact list (one short row per task: name/id + status, minimal height), not big expandable cards. - Tapping a task opens it as its OWN page/view with a Back button (not an inline expand and not a modal overlay). Use hash routing so Back works. - The task page shows all the task's fields as editable inputs plus a Save button. Editing does NOT touch anything until Save is pressed. - On Save, and only then, call the operator (POST /api/op: sync_many for edits, new_task for a brand-new task) to persist, then go Back to the list. - Keep: "+ New Project", "+ New Task" (New Task opens the same task page in create mode), per-task quick actions can live on the task page (done / lock / delete). - Use the frontend-design skill for the visual direction - make it feel intentional and clean, not a generic template, but still readable and fast on a phone. Match zProject's restrained neutral palette (see design.txt). - Must stay a single self-contained zProject_webView.html (no external assets/CDNs - the server serves just this one file).
task.requirements: compact list view; each task opens as its own back-navigable page; edits only persist via the operator when Save is pressed; new task uses the same page in create mode; single self-contained html; mobile-optimised; visual direction from the frontend-design skill
task.notes:
zProject_webView.html rewritten from scratch (still one self-contained file, no external assets). Design direction via the frontend-design skill: restrained native-utility look from design.txt - light neutral ground (#f2f2f0), one muted blue accent, hairline borders, square corners, single system-UI type family, hierarchy by weight/size only. The one deliberate device is a 3px coloured left rail on each queue row that encodes state (bug=purple, needs-attention=red, active=blue, done=green, archived/held=grey) - information, not decoration; no cards, no all-caps eyebrows, no middle-dot meta strings.
Structure: hash router (# = project picker, #<i> = that project's queue, #<i>/<taskId> or #<i>/new = a task page). The queue is a compact one-line-per-task list grouped by section; tapping a row navigates to the task's own page (real Back button + browser back both work). The task page shows every field as an editable input (name, prompt, requirements, tags, blocked-by, due, a 9-flag toggle grid, subtasks with add + done, and a collapsible agent-output/dates block) plus a sticky Save/Cancel bar and a quiet Delete. Nothing is sent until Save - it edits a deep copy so the list cache stays clean on Cancel. Save calls the operator: new_task then sync_many for a new task, sync_many for edits, plus new_subtask / subtask_done for subtask changes, then returns to the list with a toast. New Task opens the same page in create mode.
Operator/server: added new_local_project, and wired subtask_done into /api/op and the operator exe (both existed in the engine but weren't exposed). Server treats any new_*project command as a workspace reload.
Verified end to end via curl on a scratch target (new_task/sync_many/new_subtask/subtask_done/new_local_project/delete all ok); page serves and contains the routing + save wiring. Headless screenshots didn't work in this environment so the visual pass is by code review against the plan - to be eyeballed on a phone. Built app+server+operator to builds/debug + builds/release; release zipped. Committed + pushed.

task.name: archive changes
task.prompt: when a task is archived, instead of storing it in tasks.xml create a new archive.xml in the project directory and move it there to keep tasks small. this should be done by the operator. the program can still display the archives
task.notes: Archived tasks now live in a separate archive.xml in the project directory, keeping tasks.xml small. TaskXmlSerializer gained ArchiveFileName + Serialize/ToElement overloads that take an explicit task list. ProjectStore.Save partitions project.Tasks: not-archived -> tasks.xml, archived -> archive.xml (deleted when empty), Order renumbered within each file, both writes under the operator mutex. New private ReadTasksInto() reads BOTH files back into project.Tasks (archive.xml entries forced Archived=true); Load and ReloadTasks use it. Legacy migration: if tasks.xml still has archived tasks inline, Load/ReloadTasks re-save immediately to split them - so opening the app or any operator call migrates a project once, automatically. A broken archive.xml flags the project like a broken tasks.xml (Save won't clobber it). The app still shows the Archived section (archived tasks are in project.Tasks as before); the server orders tasks by section then Order. zProject itself migrated on the first operator run this session: tasks.xml 71 tasks -> 7 active, archive.xml -> 64 archived, no loss. Verified on a scratch project: archive moves a task tasks.xml->archive.xml, unarchive moves it back and removes the empty archive.xml, read works throughout; app launches against the split files. The explicit `archive`/`get_archive` operator verbs are ZP-72.

subtasks.subtask: read archive "get_archive" returns the whole archive
move to archive "archive task_id" marks a task as not in project, done, and archived and moves it to the archive
ai lock "agent_lock task_id key" locks the task by an agent
ai unlock "agent_unlock task_id key" unlocks a task if the id matches
get tag "get_tag task_id tag" returns the value of the requested tag if it exists
